newsitem.title: CHINA: Sithe gains financing for China power project.
newsitem.headline: Sithe gains financing for China power project.

text.p: Sithe China Holdings Ltd said on Friday it had obtained $128.4 million in non-recourse financing for a 100-megawatt coal-fired cogeneration power plant in north China.

A banking consortium consisting of Japan's Sumitomo Bank Ltd, Korea Exchange Bank and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell was underwriting the financing, which is not secured by any sovereign or corporate guarantees or export credits, Sithe China officials said.

"The financing for this landmark project is a vote of confidence for China's developing power market," said William Kriegel, chairman of Sithe Energies Inc, a U.S.-based power plant producer and one of three shareholders in Sithe China.
Twelve banks joined the three arrangers and the financing for the power plant in Tangshan in Hebei province was oversubscribed at $147 million, said Sithe China senior vice president James Spencer.
The debt is secured by a termination agreement executed with a Tangshan-owned power plant and further supported by a political risk policy issued by the People's Insurance Co of China, Spencer said.
Other terms of the financing were not given.
The first phase of 50 megawatts was expected to be ready in early 1997 and the rest of the project would be completed in 23 months.
Sithe China has a 60 percent stake in the plant while the Tangshan municipal government holds the remaining 40 percent.

Sithe China is jointly owned by Sithe Energies, the Government of Singapore Investment Corp and a $1 billion fund set up by insurer American International Group Inc to invest in infrastructure projects in Asia.
French conglomerate Compagnie Generale des Eaux is the largest shareholder of Sithe Energies.
Raytheon-Ebasco Overseas Ltd, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Raytheon Group, will build the power plant, which will utilise domestic equipment, officials said.

The project will provide electricity to North China Power Group, China's third largest power grid, under a 20-year power purchase agreement and thermal energy to Tangshan's thermal heating network now under construction, officials said.
The power plant will be operated by an affiliate of Sithe Energies, they said.
The Asian Development Bank has provided $30 million to build the heating network.
